guidance.coverage: Operational synopsis. Follow the guide for release selection, supported paths and post-upgrade workload observations. Detailed input and effective permission coverage is not declared.

guidance.coverage: Host-operation synopsis, not artifact qualification or a complete input contract. Installer identity, host health and downstream AIO health require their separate evidence.
effects: Delivers a privileged host worker through Arc Run Command and can reboot the machine.
The parent waits on worker state. Launcher completion is not worker completion, and the wait does not compare run IDs.
guidance.outcome: Bootstrap an AKS Edge Essentials cluster through an Arc-enabled Windows host.
prerequisites: An Arc-enabled Windows host meeting the guide's requirements, with the required managed-identity permissions and resource providers.
Explicit host and cluster configuration, target-side installer review and approval for reboots.
removal: Use the operator guide's phase-specific remediation and cleanup. Do not treat reapplication as a general rollback.

guidance.coverage: Operational synopsis. Platform readiness does not establish AIO workload health. Detailed host constraints and recovery requirements remain in the operator guide.
effects: Runs target-side upgrade work and can interrupt workloads during node VM reboot.

guidance.outcome: Upgrade an existing AKS Edge Essentials cluster through its Arc-enabled host.

An approved maintenance window and access for potential console remediation.
removal: Follow the documented failure phase and remediation path before retrying. There is no general rollback.

guidance.coverage: Enablement synopsis. The guide owns vault selection and preservation settings. Secret values and effective permissions are not inspected or exported.
effects: Can create or configure identity, vault, federation, permissions and Secret Provider Class resources, and update the instance.
Enablement is separate from materializing selected secret values in Kubernetes.
guidance.outcome: Enable workload-identity-backed Secret Sync on an existing AIO instance.
prerequisites: An existing AIO instance and cluster with OIDC issuer and workload identity enabled.
A configured Site, instance name, release selection and permissions for identities, vault resources and role assignments as applicable.
removal: Remove only the identities, permissions, data and synchronized resources you own. Configuration removal is not automatic cleanup.

guidance.coverage: Composition synopsis. Review both component guides and observe host, AIO readiness and workload outcomes separately.
effects: Combines privileged host work, possible reboots and AIO resource deployment.

guidance.outcome: Bootstrap the host, wait for worker state, then install AIO fundamentals.

A configured Site identifying the intended host and resulting cluster.
removal: Follow each component's ownership and cleanup guidance. There is no combined rollback.

guidance.outcome: Install AIO and the composed OPC UA-to-cloud example on a fresh cluster.
